solutionCodeJson.name: answers.md
solutionCodeJson.code:
# Multiprocessors 1 — UMA, NUMA, spin locks and scheduling (concepts) — answer key

1. What is the difference between a multiprocessor and a multicomputer?Multiprocessor khác multicomputer ở chỗ nào?
   Answer: b) A multiprocessor shares one memory; a multicomputer has private memories and passes messages
   Shared-memory (multiprocessor) versus message passing (multicomputer, cluster).VI: Bộ nhớ chung (multiprocessor) so với truyền thông điệp (multicomputer, cluster).

2. Why is a plain test-and-set spin lock bad on a multiprocessor?Vì sao spin lock test-and-set thuần tuý kém trên multiprocessor?
   Answer: c) Every spin writes the shared word, so the cache line bounces between cores
   Test-and-test-and-set spins on a cached read and writes only when the lock looks free.VI: Test-and-test-and-set quay trên bản đọc đã cache và chỉ ghi khi khoá có vẻ rảnh.

3. Gang scheduling means …Gang scheduling nghĩa là …
   Answer: a) all threads of a group run at the same time on different CPUs
   Communicating threads then do not wait for a thread that is descheduled.VI: Các luồng giao tiếp với nhau không phải chờ một luồng đang bị tạm dừng.

4. “CPU affinity” (processor affinity) lets the scheduler …“CPU affinity” cho phép bộ lập lịch …
   Answer: c) keep a thread on the same core to reuse its warm cache
   Moving a thread loses its cache contents (cold start).VI: Chuyển luồng sang lõi khác làm mất nội dung cache (khởi động nguội).

5. In a symmetric multiprocessing (SMP) OS …Trong hệ điều hành đa xử lý đối xứng (SMP) …
   Answer: b) every CPU can run kernel and user code and all share one copy of the OS
   Master–slave designs make CPU 0 a bottleneck; SMP needs fine-grained locking in the kernel.VI: Thiết kế master–slave làm CPU 0 thành nút cổ chai; SMP cần khoá hạt mịn trong kernel.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml:
Answer key / Đáp án

  1. b) A multiprocessor shares one memory; a multicomputer has private memories and passes messages

    Shared-memory (multiprocessor) versus message passing (multicomputer, cluster).

    VI: Bộ nhớ chung (multiprocessor) so với truyền thông điệp (multicomputer, cluster).

  2. c) Every spin writes the shared word, so the cache line bounces between cores

    Test-and-test-and-set spins on a cached read and writes only when the lock looks free.

    VI: Test-and-test-and-set quay trên bản đọc đã cache và chỉ ghi khi khoá có vẻ rảnh.

  3. a) all threads of a group run at the same time on different CPUs

    Communicating threads then do not wait for a thread that is descheduled.

    VI: Các luồng giao tiếp với nhau không phải chờ một luồng đang bị tạm dừng.

  4. c) keep a thread on the same core to reuse its warm cache

    Moving a thread loses its cache contents (cold start).

    VI: Chuyển luồng sang lõi khác làm mất nội dung cache (khởi động nguội).

  5. b) every CPU can run kernel and user code and all share one copy of the OS

    Master–slave designs make CPU 0 a bottleneck; SMP needs fine-grained locking in the kernel.

    VI: Thiết kế master–slave làm CPU 0 thành nút cổ chai; SMP cần khoá hạt mịn trong kernel.

cauHoi.de:
What is the difference between a multiprocessor and a multicomputer?

Multiprocessor khác multicomputer ở chỗ nào?

luaChon.noiDung: A multicomputer has one CPU per memory bank; a multiprocessor has one CPU in total
A multiprocessor shares one memory; a multicomputer has private memories and passes messages
A multiprocessor has no caches at all; a multicomputer shares one cache between its nodes
There is no difference; both share one memory and communicate by messages

cauHoi.giaiThich:
Shared-memory (multiprocessor) versus message passing (multicomputer, cluster).

VI: Bộ nhớ chung (multiprocessor) so với truyền thông điệp (multicomputer, cluster).

cauHoi.de:
Why is a plain test-and-set spin lock bad on a multiprocessor?

Vì sao spin lock test-and-set thuần tuý kém trên multiprocessor?

luaChon.noiDung: It needs the lock word on disk, so every spin waits for the disk to answer
It works only with two threads, so a third one enters the critical region
Every spin writes the shared word, so the cache line bounces between cores
It cannot lock anything, because the instruction is not atomic across several cores

cauHoi.giaiThich:
Test-and-test-and-set spins on a cached read and writes only when the lock looks free.

VI: Test-and-test-and-set quay trên bản đọc đã cache và chỉ ghi khi khoá có vẻ rảnh.

luaChon.noiDung: all threads of a group run at the same time on different CPUs
threads of a group are scheduled in random order on one CPU
one thread of a group gets all the CPUs in turn
the OS ignores groups and runs each thread on its own schedule

cauHoi.giaiThich:
Communicating threads then do not wait for a thread that is descheduled.

VI: Các luồng giao tiếp với nhau không phải chờ một luồng đang bị tạm dừng.

cauHoi.de:
“CPU affinity” (processor affinity) lets the scheduler …

“CPU affinity” cho phép bộ lập lịch …

luaChon.noiDung: disable the TLB of a thread that moves between cores
change the page size of a thread to fit the cache of its core
keep a thread on the same core to reuse its warm cache
run copies of one thread on every core at the same time

cauHoi.giaiThich:
Moving a thread loses its cache contents (cold start).

VI: Chuyển luồng sang lõi khác làm mất nội dung cache (khởi động nguội).

cauHoi.de:
In a symmetric multiprocessing (SMP) OS …

Trong hệ điều hành đa xử lý đối xứng (SMP) …

luaChon.noiDung: only CPU 0 runs the kernel and the other CPUs run only user code
every CPU can run kernel and user code and all share one copy of the OS
each CPU has its own copy of the OS and its own private memory
one special CPU runs all the user code and the others only the kernel

cauHoi.giaiThich:
Master–slave designs make CPU 0 a bottleneck; SMP needs fine-grained locking in the kernel.

VI: Thiết kế master–slave làm CPU 0 thành nút cổ chai; SMP cần khoá hạt mịn trong kernel.

exercises.title: Multiprocessors 2 — Speed-up and parallel efficiency
exercises.problemHtml:
Amdahl speed-up = 1 / ((1 − f) + f / n). Parallel efficiency = speed-up / n. Give both (speed-up with 2 decimals, efficiency in percent rounded to the nearest integer, digits only).

This set has 1 table. There is nothing to run: answer in the panel on the right and press Submit. The questions follow the style of the OSG202 final exam, so work them out on paper first, exactly as you would in the exam hall.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Multiprocessors 3 — The omega network: stages and switches
exercises.problemHtml:
An omega switching network connects n CPUs to n memories with 2×2 switches arranged in log₂(n) stages of n/2 switches each. Give the number of stages and the total number of switches (a crossbar would need n² crosspoints).

This set has 1 table. There is nothing to run: answer in the panel on the right and press Submit. The questions follow the style of the OSG202 final exam, so work them out on paper first, exactly as you would in the exam hall.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Mạng chuyển mạch omega nối n CPU với n bộ nhớ bằng các công tắc 2×2 xếp thành log₂(n) tầng, mỗi tầng n/2 công tắc. Cho số tầng và tổng số công tắc (crossbar cần n² điểm nối).

Bộ này có 1 bảng. Không có gì để chạy: trả lời trong khung bên phải rồi bấm Nộp. Câu hỏi theo phong cách đề FE của môn OSG202, nên hãy giải ra giấy trước như khi ngồi phòng thi.

# Multiprocessors 3 — The omega network: stages and switches — answer key

1. Omega network sizeKích thước mạng omega
   - n4.s: 2
   - n4.t: 4
   - n4.x: 16
   - n8.s: 3
   - n8.t: 12
   - n8.x: 64
   - n16.s: 4
   - n16.t: 32
   - n16.x: 256
   - n64.s: 6
   - n64.t: 192
   - n64.x: 4096
   n=4: 2 stages × 2 = 4 switches vs 16 crosspoints; n=8: 3 stages × 4 = 12 switches vs 64 crosspoints; n=16: 4 stages × 8 = 32 switches vs 256 crosspoints; n=64: 6 stages × 32 = 192 switches vs 4096 crosspoints. The omega network grows as n·log n instead of n², but it can block: two requests may need the same internal link.VI: n=4: 2 tầng × 2 = 4 công tắc so với 16 điểm nối; n=8: 3 tầng × 4 = 12 công tắc so với 64 điểm nối; n=16: 4 tầng × 8 = 32 công tắc so với 256 điểm nối; n=64: 6 tầng × 32 = 192 công tắc so với 4096 điểm nối. Mạng omega tăng như n·log n thay vì n², nhưng có thể bị chặn: hai yêu cầu có thể cần cùng một liên kết trong.

The omega network grows as n·log n instead of n², but it can block: two requests may need the same internal link.
